explain.say: A spacecraft returning from orbit hits the air at about 28,000 kilometres per hour. The air in front cannot get out of the way, so it is squashed into a shock wave and heats to thousands of degrees.

faq.q: Why does re-entry get so hot?
faq.a: The spacecraft moves so fast that the air in front is squashed far faster than it can flow away. Squashing a gas heats it, and the air in the shock wave reaches thousands of degrees.
asks: Is re-entry heat caused by friction?

faq.q: Why are capsules blunt instead of pointed?
faq.a: A blunt shape makes a strong shock wave that stands off in front of the capsule. The hottest gas stays in that layer, so less heat reaches the surface. A sharp nose would get much hotter.
asks: Why are space capsules shaped like that?

faq.q: What is an ablative heat shield?
faq.a: It is a shield designed to wear away slowly. As its surface chars and erodes, it carries heat off with it and leaves a cooler layer of gas, protecting the craft. It is used only once.
asks: Why do heat shields burn away?

faq.q: How hot does a heat shield get?
faq.a: Orion's heat shield faces about 2,800 degrees Celsius when coming back from the Moon, roughly half as hot as the surface of the Sun.
The air around a returning spacecraft gets so hot it becomes glowing, electrically charged gas called plasma, which blocks radio signals. Contact is lost for a few minutes until the craft slows down.
asks: Why do astronauts lose radio contact during re-entry?

facts: Orion's heat shield is designed for about 2,800 degrees Celsius on return from the Moon.
Re-entry heating is caused mostly by compressing the air in front of the spacecraft, not by friction.

quiz.say: What mainly heats a spacecraft during re-entry?

options.show: Air squashed in front of it
options.say: Air squashed in front of it

quiz.why: The craft squashes the air ahead into a shock wave, and compressing gas that hard heats it to thousands of degrees.

wrong.1: Sunlight warms it a little, but the fierce heat comes from compressed air.
wrong.2: Capsules usually coast through re-entry with their main engines off.
